# Calmar ratio (`calmar_ratio`)

*Category: Risk-adjusted performance · Nature: derived · Unit: ratio · Formula id: `calmar_ratio@v1` · Methodology 0.1.0*

## 1. What does it measure?

Annualized return per unit of maximum drawdown.

## 2. Formula

```text
CAGR / |max drawdown|
```

## 3. Required inputs

Periodic simple returns with a regular frequency.

## 4. Is higher or lower better?

Higher is better.

## 5. Plain-language interpretation

How much yearly return was earned relative to the worst peak-to-trough loss.

## 6. Professional interpretation

Young (1991) defined Calmar on a trailing 36-month window; OpenFactsheet canonically uses the full history so that no window is chosen. Maximum drawdown grows with history length, so values fall as track records lengthen.

## 7. Assumptions

- Full-history window.
- Risk-free rate 0%.

## 8. When can it be misleading?

- Histories of different lengths are compared.
- The maximum drawdown is a single unrepresentative event.

## 9. Minimum sensible data

At least 2 observations and a non-zero drawdown; low confidence below 3 years. (policy `ratio_standard`: Risk-adjusted ratios: at least 2 observations; low confidence below 3 years, moderate below 5 years.)

## 11. Sources

- Young, T. W. (1991). Calmar Ratio: A Smoother Tool. Futures, 20(1), 40.
- Bacon, C. R. (2021). Practical Risk-Adjusted Performance Measurement (2nd ed.). Wiley.

## 12. OpenFactsheet convention

Full history, geometric CAGR, signed max drawdown in absolute value (decision 0009).
